This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petitions filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V.
Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and 3 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 Rs.30,00,000/- due to the injuries sustained by them, in a road traffic accident.
2.
These two petitions are arising out of the same accident.
Hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion, for the sake of convenience and to avoid the repetition.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL *
3. Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition averments that, on the fateful date of the alleged accident, on 22.12.2021 at about 8.20 p.m., the petitioners were proceeding as pedestrians on the left side of Kunigal-Nelamangala NH-75 Highway road, slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near Kunigal-Nelamangala NH-75 highway road, Yantaganahalli Village, near Malgudi Mailari Mane Hotel, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the Splendor bike bearing registration No.KA-12-K- 4 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 3696, came from Kunigal and dashed against the petitioners.
As a result, the petitioners were fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

4. It is stated in the petition that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner of MVC No.710/2022 was shifted to V.P. Magnus Hospital, then shifted to K.C. General hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took the treatment as an inpatient.
For his medical expenses and other incidental expenses, he had spent Rs.2,00,000/- and got permanent disability due to the injuries sustained by him.

5. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, petitioner of MVC 711/2022 was shifted to V.P. Magnus Hospital, then shifted to K.C. General Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, the petitioner Shankar Ree vs Krishnappa on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13578985/
2 took the treatment as an inpatient.
For his medical expenses and other incidental expenses, he had spent more 5 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 than Rs.3,00,000/- and got permanent disability due to the injuries sustained by him.

6. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner in MVC 710/2022, was hale and healthy, and working as a labour at Estate, Yantaganahalli and used to earn Rs.19,500/- per month, and used to utilize the said amount, for the maintenance of his family.
Due to this, unfortunate accident, the petitioner has suffered mentally and physically, as well as financially.

7. It is stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner of MVC 711/2022, was hale and healthy, and working as a labour at Estate, Yantaganahalli and used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month, and used to utilize the said amount, for the maintenance of his family.
Due to this, unfortunate accident, the petitioner has suffered mentally and physically, as well as financially. .
It is alleged in the petitions that, the accident had taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Splendor bike bearing registration No.KA-12-K-3696.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have filed both petitions claiming compensation in the case on hand.
9. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, respondents have appeared through the counsel, but, in spite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1, have not filed his written statement.
Therefore, written statement of the respondent No.1 was taken as not filed.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2, has filed the written statement in answer to the case of the petitioner.

10. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident, and the 7 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 injuries sustained by the petitioners in the said accident, in question.
But, seriously denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

It is the main contention of the respondent No.2 that, alleged accident had occurred, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioners, as they were crossing the road negligently, which caused the accident and its consequences.

The respondent, though not disputed about the issuance of the policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA- 12-K-3696, contended that,
the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) & Section 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.

It is another contention that, the rider of the offending vehicle had 8 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle, and the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

17.

It is the case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, Splendor bike bearing registration No.KA-12-K-3696, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the respective petitioners had sustained injuries in the said accident.

18. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle though appeared before the court, not made an effort to challenge the case of the petitioner, by filing written statement and by adducing evidence.

The respondent No.2, insurance company, though not disputed the accident in question, and the injuries sustained by the 13 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 &
711/2022 respective petitioners

, seriously disputed the allegation of actionable negligence, on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, stating that, due to the negligence on the part of the respective petitioners, accident in question and its consequences had taken place.

19. At the time of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners, canvassed the point that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory evidence to prove the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, consequently, the petitioners had sustained injuries.

Per contra, it is the strong contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company, that, the petitioners were crossing the road, in a drunken condition, in the place wherein, not provided access for crossing the road, on the highway, in a negligent manner.
Further, as per the sketch, they were in the middle of the road, at the time of 14 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 accident.
As such, both the petitioners are solely responsible for accident and its consequences.
20. On going through the above issues, burden is on the petitioners, to prove the same, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitioners, relied on their respective affidavit evidence, and examined as PW1 & PW2.

21. In the affidavit evidence of both the petitioners, Shahid Khan and Shankar Ree, had reiterated the averments made in the main petition.
On the other hand, the respondent company, in counter to the evidence of the Petitioners, relied on the evidence of the rider of the offending vehicle, by name Lingappa as RW1.

In the evidence of the said witness,
deposed that, on the fateful day of the accident, he was proceeding in the offending vehicle, on the highway, at that time, the petitioners, by consuming the alcohol, negligently were crossing the divider, and suddenly, came towards the offending vehicle, which caused accident and its consequences.
Further, deposed that, at the time of the accident, Jeep and Car were there, and he shifted the injured petitioners to the hospital, by calling ambulance.

In support of all these defenses,
except the production of R.C and D.L, no other documentary evidence placed on record, for consideration.

22. On taking birds eye view towards the material documents placed by the respective 16 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 petitioners, noted above, evident that, accident in question had taken place on 22.12.2021.

On the basis of first information given by the petitioner Shankar Ree on 23.12.2021, criminal law set in motion against the rider of the offending vehicle, Motor Cycle bearing registration No. KA-12-K-3696, alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

In connection with the one day delay in giving first information is concerned, there is clear narration in column No. 3(C) of the Ex.P.1 and in the Ex.P.2, that, the complainant was taking treatment in Nelamangala Hospital, in the said hospital, he gave first information about the accident, before the police.
As such, there is no much delay in fiving first information and the injured/complainant gave his statement, in the hospital.
As such, to suspect about the recitals of the first information, no contra evidence available on 17 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 record.
Accordingly, one day delay in giving first information is not fatal in the case on hand.

23. It is relevant to note that, in the recitals of the complaint, there is a clear narration about the actionable negligence committed by the rider of the offending vehicle, on the fateful day of the accident.
The said material document remained unchallenged either by the respondent No.1, or the rider of the offending vehicle, well in time, before the competent court of law.

Even not made an effort to give complaint against the petitioners, if at all the alleged accident was due to the mistake on the part of the petitioners, to believe the entire defense forthcoming in the written statement, as well as in the evidence of the RW1.
Hence, I am of the view that, there are no suspicious circumstances to disbelieve the recitals of the Ex.P1 & Ex.P2.
Another document, Ex.P.3, statement of the injured Shahidh also, substantiates 18 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 the recitals of the Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and the case of the petitioners.

sentences.text: In order to test the veracity of the evidence of the witnesses let me to discuss the cross examination portion, for better appreciation of the evidence placed on record, in toto.

At the time of the cross examination of the PW1 and PW2, learned counsel for the respondent company, put several questions and suggestions, to prove the innocence of the rider of the offending vehicle, and to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement.

Both 23 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 &
711/2022 the witnesses were denied the suggestion that, while crossing the road, alleged accident had taken place.

Though there were some admissions at the time of the cross examination of the PW2, in continuation of the same, answered that, while crossing the road, both the petitioners were watching the movements of the vehicles from both side.
At the same time, though it was admitted that, in the Ex.P.12, there is a mention of non MLC, on going through the wound certificates, and discharge summery, substantiate the history of RTA.
Over all appreciation of the answers given by these two petitioners, will not helpful to believe the defenses of the company, since no material points culled out in support of the said defenses.

Apart from this, at the time of cross examination of the PW3 and PW4, some of the answers elicited with respect to the vehicle, but the police notice under section 133 of MV Act, and reply to the said notice, along with the recitals 24 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 of the police documents, especially final report and the discharge summery,
there is a clear whisper about the involvement of the two wheeler in the accident.

29. On the other hand, at the time of the cross examination of the RW1, answers given by him, goes to show that, he is not disputing the accident, and also about the presence of the offending vehicle in the accident.
But, to substantiate his answer that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioners alleged accident had taken place, no supportive evidence is available on record.
Even no evidence to prove that, as on the date of the accident, the petitioners were in drunken condition.

When the respondent company, is denying the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, through Ex.P12 and the answers given in support of the same by the PW3 and PW4, why the answers of RW1, is contrary to the said stand, by admitting the presence of the vehicle in the scene of 25 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 occurrence and also, he answered that, he had shifted the injured persons to the hospital.
Hence, I am of the considered view that, both the petitioners have adduced satisfactory evidence in connection with the above issue.
On the other hand, no cogent evidence to show that, the petitioners have engineered the documentary evidence, to gain wrongful compensation, from the respondents.

30. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by way of affidavit evidence and the documentary evidence, speak that, the petitioners have paced satisfactory evidence to prove the above issues, to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the Splendor bike bearing registration No.KA-12-K-3696.

Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending 26 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 &

answers given by the witness and denial of some suggestions evident that, till today, the petitioner is suffering slight problem in connection with the injuries.

34 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 Finally he denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability in higher side only to help the petitioner.

42. Over all appreciation of the evidence of PW5, along with the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, reveals that, in connection with whole body disability of the petitioner, percentage of disability assessed by the PW5, is little bit exorbitant.
Hence, it is apt to take the whole body disability of the petitioner as 12% instead of 18%.
The same will meet the ends of justice.
43. In connection with the age of the petitioner by name Shahid Khan is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 29 years.

The said document remained unquestioned.
Hence, as on the date of accident, age of the petitioner was 29 years.
To the said age, as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '17' is to be taken into consideration.

44. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examination-in-chief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was working as a Labour at Vegan Estate, Yantaganahalli and was getting an income of Rs.19,500/-
per month.
In support of this, there is no iota of documents to show his definite income per month.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income has to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
And also, it is apt to rely on the chart prepared by the 36 SCCH-18 MVC 710/2022 & 711/2022 legal services authority, with respect to the notional income.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, I am of the view that, in the light of all the facts and circumstances of the present case, fully discussed above it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.

definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.

disability, definitely the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work.

52. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence,
